judgements.justification: Both committees named the thin experiments (two toy benchmarks, NODE and penalty baselines, no gas spread); A called them 'can be further improved' and gave a spotlight, B rejected on 'insufficient empirical evidence'.
B's two-sentence meta-review rejected a 3/6/7/5 split because 'one reviewer is still strongly convinced about rejection', with no assessment of its own.
B's Reviewer_DeZu cut 7 to 6 citing weaknesses 'other reviewers have noted', not the rebuttal.
The authors misread AB4a's degeneracy question twice and AB4a dropped 6 to 5; DeZu offered to return to 7 and got no reply.
B's Reviewer_D146 gave 5 after 2 hours on assertion ('not as exciting') and never replied to the response; the 5 counted.
B's final positions 3/6/7/5 have only two of four at or above threshold, so the rejection was not against a positive majority.
B's AC stated no positive assessment and did not decide by a mean threshold; it followed the detractor.
xSwS's 3 rests on central empirical points (benchmarks, baselines, spread), not a peripheral detail.
Both committees read the paper as a methods contribution, an exact parameterization of GENERIC brackets.
A's raisers were at confidence 4 and hnow checked [42] himself; no reviewer said the core was beyond their expertise.
Both committees asked for stronger experiments; the gap is the weight given to a shared concern, not an extra requirement.
No reviewer's praise rested on a wrong factual claim about the paper.
xSwS's main concern, insufficient empirical evidence, was never resolved; he had no criticism of the parameterization from the start.
A's DqnY raised 'based on the assumption that the missing information will be added', while B rejected on the evidence as submitted despite the same promised error bars.
B's AB4a wrote 'I increased my rating to 7' but the form still shows 5, and B's AC counted the 7.
Neither AC brought in an off-record reviewer.
xSwS's clarity complaint was a weak side point and the notes show no expertise gap behind it; all six other reviewers praised the writing.
AB4a's raise to 7 came with a stated reason, the high-dimensional GENERIC examples.
No AC set aside a silent detractor; D146's unengaged 5 counted in B.
A's top scorer PQY3 (8) never joined the discussion or argued for the paper.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper.
No reviewer contested the GENERIC premise; xSwS had 'no criticisms of the proposed parameterization'.
A's meta-review argued only 'a clear accept', conceded the experiments 'can be further improved', and gave no reason for the spotlight.
Reviewers in both committees named missing baselines from the literature (DqnY in A; xSwS, DeZu in B).
Neither meta-review misstated final positions; B's AC correctly counted AB4a's declared 7.
No reviewer or AC objected to a narrow audience; D146's point was about significance of entropy, not breadth.
No misreading detractor held a chair to arguing only acceptance; B rejected.
No new experiments were posted to either forum; A got promises and a code link, B examples of systems.
Neither committee had a lone high-confidence expert outweighed by low-confidence reviews; most confidences were 3 to 4.
DeZu's cut came in the discussion period with an open offer the authors could have answered; no objection arrived after responses closed.
B's lower ratings came with more negative text (xSwS, D146), so the gap is judgement, not scoring leniency.
No one judged the headline claim or title overstated.
No committee's reviewers converged on marginal-accept at low confidence; A rated 7/6/8 at confidence 4.
